name: ztpf_reorder_profile_steps
why: Reorder with a hidden dependency. Swapping the routing-table capture ahead of the status capture (before AND after the upgrade) moves steps 1<->2 and 4<->5 -- and the two diff steps reference those by NUMBER (`diff_steps: 1,4` / `2,5`). A reorder that only rewrites stepSequence leaves both diffs comparing the wrong captures; the right edit also swaps their diff_steps.
Nothing is added or removed: still 7 steps, contiguous.

Graded on the WORLD (`world_after`): the bundle is `writable`, each approved card applies, and the resulting records are read back. Card-level graders pass a build with an invented action link, duplicate stepSequence, or a copied firmware version; this does not.

Moves go through the `Move Step Number on Automation Profile` playbook (it renumbers every step); the two diff steps' stepARGS are the approved writes read back, so min_writes is 2. The order and the args are graded on the records, however they were written.

EXPECTED TO FAIL until the ZTPF content is fixed: `Move Step Number on Automation Profile` renumbers stepSequence but not the stepARGS position refs, so a UI move breaks the diffs too. The fix belongs in that playbook (rewrite `*step*` numbers through the same old->new map), not in the assistant.

steps.user: Reorder this profile so the routing table is captured before the system status, both before and after the upgrade.
